Choose a ZIP, or a clip and its receipt.

    What this proves

    The video file is exactly the file the camera's QoreWitness recorded. Not one byte was changed. It existed at the time shown, because its fingerprint was written to a public record (QoreChain test network) and signed by the camera.

    What it cannot prove

    It does not prove who is in the video or that the scene was real. It does not prove who owns the camera. The camera clock sets the recording time, and the seal time comes from the public record. QoreWitness is in beta on the QoreChain test network, which can be reset, and a seal is not a legal timestamp.

    Technical details
    QoreChain testnet (diana, chain ID 9800). A blockchain record is not an eIDAS qualified timestamp. It proves that the file existed at a time. It does not prove who recorded it or that the scene was real.
